why: The default answer for any reference with no more specific mapping.
NO MAPPING IN THIS DIRECTORY MATCHES ON A CURRENCY, in a request body or
anywhere else -- grep for it. So this stub accepts an EUR charge and an XAF
charge identically, and which one arrives is decided entirely by the
`providers[].currency` of the config the caller loaded:
config/application.yml            mtn_momo -> EUR
config/application-sandbox.yml    (inherits) EUR
the conformance suite             EUR, configured in Rust
.e2e/application-demo.yml         XAF, since 2026-09-04 (Step 9, lane 4)
EUR IS THE SANDBOX'S TRUTH AND IT HAS NOT CHANGED: MTN's real sandbox
rejects XAF (docs/flows/money.md), which is why the first three above say
EUR and why the demo overlay is the only one that does not. The demo
overlay differs because the demo shop (examples/shop) prices its catalogue
in XAF and offers a payer both rails, and vpay refuses a confirm whose rail
settles in another currency than the intent.
The `currency` and `amount` in the response body below are therefore NOT a
claim about what MTN accepts, and they are not read by vpay at all:
`vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::wire::StatusResponse` deserialises `status`,
`reason` and `financialTransactionId` and nothing else. They are here
because MTN's documented status body carries them, and they are spelled the
way the SANDBOX would spell them.

mappings.name: status: the rail has no record of this reference

metadata.why: `not_found_is_never_on_its_own_a_failure`: a push rail can answer 404 for a charge it is about to accept, so this must be ChargeStatus::NotFound and never Failed.

mappings.name: status: declined — the payer had no balance
status: declined — the payer never entered their PIN

reason.message: The transaction could not be performed

metadata.why: -> payer_timeout. Deliberately the object-shaped `reason`: MTN documents both shapes and the adapter must read either.

mappings.name: status: declined — our own partner account is not allowed

metadata.why: -> provider_account_blocked, the one decline in the table that pages (docs/flows/failures.md).
`an_unavailable_rail_is_a_transport_error_never_a_decline`: Transport, Category::Rail — a rail that is down must not look like a payer who was declined.

mappings.name: status: answered, but far too slowly

metadata.why: Two orders of magnitude above the suite's SHORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (100 ms), so the assertion is about ProviderConfig::request_timeout firing and not about a slow CI machine. The body is a *success* on purpose: the adapter must fail on the deadline, not on the content.

mappings.name: status: a body far larger than any answer this rail documents

why: REF_HUGE. 300 KB, comfortably past vpay_provider::http::MAX_RAIL_BODY_BYTES (256
KiB). Response::text()/bytes() read to end of stream, so before the Step 3 security
review the peer chose how much memory a worker task allocated -- one task per charge,
each willing to buffer whatever arrived. bounded_body stops at the cap and the
adapter answers Malformed naming it.
The body is a valid, SUCCESSFUL status on purpose: if the bound were removed the
adapter would parse it and answer Succeeded, so the case cannot pass for the wrong
reason. Padded via --global-response-templating rather than a 300 KB fixture file,
which is not a thing to check into a repository.

mappings.name: status: declined — the prompt's own window closed

why: -> payer_timeout. MTN publishes `EXPIRED` in `ErrorReason.code` (the Collection
API's OpenAPI components, retrieved 2026-09-10 -- see
vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping's header). It is the second reason on this rail
that means payer_timeout, the other being COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION at
...0f02, and the two are kept apart here so that the mapping of EACH is proven
rather than the mapping of whichever one a test happened to pick.
NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH demo-outcomes.json, WHICH IS STILL RIGHT: MTN's *status*
vocabulary is PENDING / SUCCESSFUL / FAILED and has no EXPIRED. This is a
`reason` on a FAILED status, which is a different field and a different
enumeration. Orange's EXPIRED is a *status*.

mappings.name: status: declined — the payer refused the prompt

why: -> payer_declined, AND THIS IS THE ROW ISSUE #59 EXISTS FOR. Until 2026-09-10
FailureCode::PayerDeclined was defined by vpay-core, given buyer copy by
examples/shop, listed in the SDKs' types -- and produced by NO adapter. The shop
said so in as many words ('produced by no adapter in this repository'), which
was true and was the wrong thing to be true.
PAYMENT_NOT_APPROVED is published by MTN in ErrorReason.code, AND ErrorReason is
the type MTN gives the very field this stub is filling in: RequestToPayResult
declares reason as $ref ErrorReason, and RequesttoPayTransactionStatus
(GET /v1_0/requesttopay/{referenceId}) answers RequestToPayResult on its 200.
So this body's shape is the documented one and this reason is a documented
value of it.
Corrected 2026-09-11. These lines previously said that 'what is NOT published is
which operations return it: ErrorReason is the whole Collection API's error
schema, not requesttopay's', and called the row a deliberate assumption. The
portal's own operation document says otherwise; the claim was not re-read before
it was written down in four places.
What is still unproven is that MTN ever SENDS it. A schema types a field; it
does not promise a value, and nothing in this repository has called MTN. If the
reason never arrives the mapping row is dead code; if it does, a payer reads
'the prompt was declined' instead of 'the rail refused and did not say why'.

mappings.name: status: declined — the payer rejected the approval

why: -> payer_declined, by the same published enum and the same reasoning as ...0f05.
Deliberately the BARE STRING shape where 0f05 uses the object, so that both of
MTN's documented `reason` shapes are exercised over the wire for this code and
not only for payer_timeout (which has the same pairing at 0f01/0f02).
A separate reference rather than a second body on 0f05 because the two are
separate published codes: flattening them here would mean the suite proved one
mapping and the doc's table claimed two.

mappings.name: status: declined — the rail has no such payer

why: -> invalid_payer. Distinct from the SUBMIT-time PAYER_NOT_FOUND (a 400, mapped
through the same table by submit_outcome and steered by MSISDN in
demo-outcomes.json): this is the same reason arriving on a terminal FAILED
status, which is a different code path in the adapter and was covered by no
conformance case before 2026-09-10.

mappings.name: status: declined — the payer is over one of the rail's limits

why: -> payer_limit_reached. Payer-actionable but not immediately: the shop offers a
retry (FailureCode::payer_actionable) and the copy says 'per transaction, per
day, or per month', which is the honest answer to a limit nobody here can read.

mappings.name: status: declined — the paying wallet is not active

why: -> payer_account_blocked.
ONE OF THE TWO REASONS THIS REPOSITORY MAPS THAT MTN DOES NOT PUBLISH: it is
absent from ErrorReason.code (retrieved 2026-09-10), as is
COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION at ...0f02. Both are declared in
vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping::UNPUBLISHED_REASONS and both are kept, because
they have been in docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md and in these stubs since Step 3
and dropping them would turn two mapped declines back into provider_error. This
case proves the MAPPING, not the rail: a stub answering a string MTN may never
send proves only that the table row works.

mappings.name: status: declined — the rail has no such payee

why: -> invalid_payee. The merchant's own collection account, not the payer's: this is
one of the two merchant_actionable codes (vpay_core::FailureCode), and the shop
deliberately does NOT offer a retry on it -- a buyer pressing 'try again' would
fail identically a second time.

mappings.name: status: declined — the payee may not receive

why: -> payee_account_blocked. The other merchant_actionable code. Distinct from
NOT_ALLOWED at ...0f03, which is OUR partner account and pages instead.

mappings.name: status: declined — the rail says the service is unavailable

why: -> provider_unavailable.
DELIBERATELY NOT THE SAME THING AS ...05aa, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT.
...05aa is an HTTP 503, which is ProviderError::Transport: the charge's fate is
unknown and the poll ladder keeps asking. This is a 200 whose FAILED body names
SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, which is TERMINAL -- the rail answered, and what it said is
that the charge is dead. Same words, opposite handling, and
an_unavailable_rail_is_a_transport_error_never_a_decline covers the other one.

mappings.name: status: declined — cancelled, by nobody MTN will name

why: -> provider_error, ON PURPOSE, and this case exists to keep that a decision.
TRANSACTION_CANCELED is published in ErrorReason.code. It is NOT mapped to
payer_declined, which would read well, because MTN publishes no description
saying who cancels, and the only cancel operations on the Collection API are
CancelInvoice and CancelPreApproval -- neither of which vpay calls. Guessing 'the
payer' would put a sentence in front of a buyer on the strength of a verb.
So it lands in the fallback, and what this case asserts is the OTHER half of the
contract: the rail's own word survives into ChargeStatus::Failed's `raw`, so an
operator reading failure_raw sees TRANSACTION_CANCELED and can add the row the
day MTN answers the question. It is listed in
vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping::UNMAPPED_REASONS with the other six.
